# Complete modifier-predicate consumers before native engines

Reference `26086de87` and independent native initial memory `da839f839`
precede this consumer freeze. The three public C bodies and their integer
prototypes remain unchanged. No predicate/traversal engine exists in Go.
Use `OPENNOX_MODIFIER_PREDICATES_BEFORE=1` for this preparation source: it
checks all three old prototypes and absence of the future engine file.
The actual native-engine test branch requires all three native C prototypes.
Keep the consumer preparation local until the associated engines are added
and their final source is validated.

`observe_modifier_defend_predicate_accesses_4e03d0.py` adds observation hooks
to an in-memory copy of the immutable producer. It first checks the original
producer's SHA-256, then reproduces both complete original output bytes
exactly. The original producer, independent inputs and canonical output are
unchanged. Both original FPU profiles record the same 1,411 ordered external
memory accesses, including each attempted faulting access and its original
instruction. The sidecar's encoded/decoded SHA-256 values are:

```
f8b4b5c700b802200b3d03ed286bfd36f1677384c02e5e3dbd48448087ddba59
58f0b8982be0a65f4a86748769a64b05bfac9ca79d8f823d635962715f29615b
```

The initial unfrozen observer omitted Unicorn's callback value argument and
fails before completing an input. Its source, logs and exit are retained in
`ART/modifier-defend-predicates-native-entry-port/first-access-observer-hook-arity-failure-v1.zip`.
Only the new observer signature is corrected; no original source, golden or
engine is changed to resolve it.

The complete consumer checks all 64 KiB of the native allocation against the
independently initialized guard plus original final deltas. A separate full
PE32 projection checks every original heap byte. Every observed scalar/output
window and native pointer token has an explicit correspondence; unrelated
native bytes remain guards. Both output aliases and the last-readable-word
domain retain the earlier initial-memory scope.

Frozen typed field getters and a DWORD store observe semantic reads/writes
before and after the actual operation. They preserve base pointers separately
from field IDs, including nil bases. Normalized access kind/address/width/
value/completion must equal the full original sequence, including its valid
prefix and final attempted fault. This is a typed-access correspondence,
without an assertion of identical physical native instruction/bus traces.
The complete original instruction remains in the immutable source sidecar.

The compiled native-engine branch also compares the actual public C root
return/fault and observed C callback identities/order. An independent C
function-pointer carrier records the real callback arguments, return and
caller-owned scratch before/after invocation. Its unrelated primitive C
control exercises six actual addresses above 4 GiB and distinct non-boolean
return/output constants. It verifies transport without implementing either
game predicate. Trace hooks are disabled by default.

The original caller windows and all original writes are consumed as source
certificates. Applying the ordered original writes must reconstruct the full
original heap and caller window exactly. The traversal's reused third
argument/loop counter is retained. The actual callback's scratch output is
compared with every original fourth-argument write. Neither physical caller
stack layout nor arbitrary aliases between a caller frame and native object
structures are claimed equivalent across ABIs.

Before any native engine, 596 transports per local configuration replay all
1,411 CPU-observed accesses for each original FPU profile on native memory,
using those accesses as data. Actual getter/store operations, ordered values,
fault prefixes and complete final heaps must agree. No game algorithm chooses
these actions. The original-source return/caller/call certificates are also
checked. There are zero native-engine comparison leaves in this phase.

Go 1.27.3 normal/strict HD each pass 1,205 events, including 298 original
initial states, 298 frozen-getter runtime cases, 596 complete transports and
the actual C callback carrier control. The 136 independent initial read
faults and three actual unchanged-C high-pointer child faults per profile
remain verified. All four parent mains are preserved before execution;
parents/drivers exit zero without forced termination. Apple Mach-O symbol
inspection confirms the complete native consumer and dynamic C call carrier
are compiled, while the three raw Go exports remain absent. Original
producers/inputs/goldens and the independent initial controls remain exact.

Evidence: `ART/modifier-defend-predicates-native-entry-port/complete-frozen-consumers-normal-and-strict-qualified-v2.json`.
Both successful preparation versions' actual mains and logs remain in
verified `local-suite-archives`; source snapshots are verified ZIPs and
temporary symbol-inspection copies are removed. Version one transports only
initial state; version two additionally replays complete access/final outputs.

Further read-only dependency analysis identifies the still-active raw
`nox_xxx_checkInversionEffect_4FA4F0` in GAME4.c. Its existing 159-byte original
seal calls parent lookup `4EC580`, then reloads the modifier callback for the
indirect call at `4FA561`. The existing ordinary Go collision helper restores
its registered-effect path; it does not close this raw two-integer C ABI.
Freeze this coupled entry's original/initial/full-consumer evidence before
porting the four related raw entries. Do not change its unsafe caller merely
to make new callback declarations compile.
